entries.name: npm package identity, bin entries, engines, workspaces
entries.purpose: FACT: package 'omniroute' v3.8.51 (MIT) ships two bin entries (omniroute -> bin/omniroute.mjs, omniroute-reset-password -> bin/reset-password.mjs), declares npm workspaces open-sse + packages/browser-pool, and gates Node to >=22.22.2 <23 || >=24.0.0 <27. The single npm package is the primary distribution unit; the CLI bin is also the MCP-stdio and recovery-tool entry.
entries.risk_class: low — identity metadata only, no runtime behavior
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `npm pack --dry-run` shows bin/files; `omniroute --version` prints 3.8.51; engine mismatch warns via bin/nodeRuntimeSupport.mjs.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Uninstall the npm package (`npm uninstall -g omniroute`); package.json:253-254 wires scripts/build/uninstall.mjs.

entries.name: Isolated Next.js standalone build
entries.purpose: FACT: `npm run build` spawns `next build` in an isolated environment (build-next-isolated.mjs runNextBuild spawns process.execPath) with output:'standalone' and distDir .build/next (NEXT_DIST_DIR overridable). Produces the self-contained server bundle every runtime mode consumes (Docker runner, electron-standalone, npm package).
entries.risk_class: medium — build host resource exhaustion class (heap/worker caps documented in Dockerfile:177-200)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: build from a clean checkout; assert .build/next/standalone/server.js exists and boots (check:pack-boot, package.json:159).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete .build/; build artifacts are regenerable. No runtime state touched.

entries.name: Build profiles: minimal (secure) and backend-only
entries.purpose: FACT: two alternate build profiles exist — OMNIROUTE_BUILD_PROFILE=minimal (build:secure) and OMNIROUTE_BUILD_BACKEND_ONLY=1 (build:backend) — selecting reduced build surfaces of the same isolated builder.
entries.risk_class: low — build-time variant selection only
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: run each profile; diff the emitted standalone tree against the full build's manifest.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not set the profile env vars; the default full build runs.

entries.name: Release build chain with build-SHA stamping
entries.purpose: FACT: build:release wipes .build/dist, stamps OMNIROUTE_BUILD_SHA from git, runs the standalone build plus the CLI tarball build, then writes the build SHA — the upstream release artifact chain.
entries.risk_class: low — build orchestration only
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: run build:release on a tagged checkout; verify the stamped SHA matches the commit.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Artifacts are regenerable; nothing persists outside .build/dist.

entries.name: CLI npm tarball prepublish + files allowlist
entries.purpose: FACT: the npm package content is governed by an explicit files allowlist (bin/, dist/, open-sse/, selected src/ subtrees, build scripts; tests excluded) and prepublish.ts (build:cli) stages dist/ via runBuildTool; prepublishOnly chains build:cli-api + build:cli + check:pack-artifact before any publish.
entries.risk_class: medium — a allowlist mistake ships or omits runtime files (publish-surface risk)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `npm pack` and diff tarball contents against the allowlist; check:pack-artifact (validate-pack-artifact.ts) must pass.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not publish; the tarball is a local artifact until `npm publish` runs.

entries.name: postinstall native-binary fixup
entries.purpose: FACT: every `npm install` of the package runs scripts/build/postinstall.mjs, which repairs platform-mismatched native binaries (better-sqlite3 et al.) shipped from the build platform, keyed off PUBLISHED_BUILD_ARCH/PLATFORM from native-binary-compat.mjs.
entries.risk_class: medium — install-time code execution on the host (supply-chain surface, runs on every install)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: install the tarball on a different platform/arch than the build; assert better-sqlite3 loads (postinstall smoke path).
entries.rollback_or_disable: `npm install --ignore-scripts` skips it (at the cost of broken native modules); uninstall removes the package.

entries.name: Pack-artifact validation and boot/install-upgrade gates
entries.purpose: FACT: three scripted gates verify the packaged artifact before publish: validate-pack-artifact.ts (check:pack-artifact / --policy-only), check-pack-boot.mjs (the packed server actually boots), and check-install-upgrade.mjs (install/upgrade path).
entries.risk_class: low — read-only verification gates
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: run the three checks against a staged dist/; all must exit 0.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Gates are advisory locally; skipping them risks shipping a broken artifact (they are the rollback).

entries.name: Standalone bundle assembler + deterministic tarballs
entries.purpose: FACT: assembleStandalone.mjs is the declared single source of truth for the standalone bundle's native assets and extra modules (EXTRA_MODULE_ENTRIES; run-standalone.mjs and the WS wrapper copied to dev/ inside the bundle), and standaloneTarball.mjs implements pure-Node deterministic ustar/gzip (zeroed mtime/uid/gid, normalized modes) so a given tree archives byte-identically on every machine.
entries.risk_class: low — build-time file staging
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: build twice on different hosts; tarball digests must match; boot the assembled bundle.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Artifacts regenerable; nothing persists.

entries.name: Optional native dependency stack
entries.purpose: FACT: heavy native/ML modules are optionalDependencies — better-sqlite3 (primary SQLite driver), keytar (OS keychain), sqlite-vec, tls-client-node, onnxruntime-node + llmlingua/transformers SLM stack — so the core install degrades gracefully when they fail to build (node:sqlite fallback per P5 core.ts:192,205).
entries.risk_class: medium — optional native builds fetch/compile at install time
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: install with and without --include=optional; verify core routes work in both modes (P5's driver fallback).
entries.rollback_or_disable: `npm install --omit=optional`; update.mjs:188-190 shows the updater force-includes them.

entries.name: Optional runtime packs (checksummed ML/browser closures)
entries.purpose: FACT: issue-#10321 Stage-7 pack system ships the heavy optional ML/browser dependency closure as versioned, checksummed packs installed on first use into DATA_DIR/packs/<name>/node_modules (manifest owns the shared contract; installer verifies; `omniroute packs` is the UX; electron prepends pack node_modules to NODE_PATH). Fail-open by design when a pack is absent.
entries.risk_class: medium — first-use network installs of versioned code into the data dir
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: install a pack via `omniroute packs`, corrupt a file, and confirm verification catches it; confirm features degrade gracefully with the pack removed.
entries.rollback_or_disable: `omniroute packs remove <name>` (installer removePack); absent packs degrade, never throw (manifest fail-open contract).

entries.name: npm publish workflow (provenance, staged 2FA publish)
entries.purpose: FACT: the upstream release channel publishes to npm from GitHub Actions with id-token provenance, a staged mode requiring owner 2FA after a staged boot-verify, optional self-hosted 'omni-release' runner, and SBOM attachment to the GitHub release. HX never publishes OmniRoute; recorded as the artifact's upstream provenance machinery (trust input to our corpus, not an HX capability).
entries.risk_class: high — external shared-state mutation (registry publish) when run upstream
entries.test_contract: Layer-N (upstream only): staged publish dry-run; verify npm provenance attestation on the published tarball.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Upstream: unpublish/deprecate window; HX: pin and content-verify the snapshot (already done, 07-source-provenance-receipt.md).

entries.name: CLI entry point with fast-path and special bypasses
entries.purpose: FACT: bin/omniroute.mjs fast-paths bare --version before loading tsx/polyfills/Commander (:47-51), redirects console output to stderr under --mcp to protect the JSON-RPC stream (:59-64), and hard-bypasses Commander for --mcp, reset-encrypted-columns, and reset-password (:302-328) before delegating all other commands to createProgram.
entries.risk_class: medium — every CLI invocation flows through this file's bootstrap side effects
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `omniroute --version` returns without DB/env side effects; `--mcp` emits protocol-clean stdout; unknown commands error via Commander.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No persistent state changed by the entry logic itself; bypass tools are covered by their own entries.

entries.name: CLI env-file loading chain + Electron server.env migration
entries.purpose: FACT: the CLI loads env vars first-set-wins from DATA_DIR/.env, default-data-dir/.env, cwd/.env, and (unless OMNIROUTE_CLI_SKIP_REPO_ENV=1) package-root/.env, warning on shadowed keys; a one-time migration copies Electron's <DATA_DIR>/server.env to .env when no .env exists (#7302) so the STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY survives a desktop-to-CLI migration.
entries.risk_class: medium — silently sources configuration/secrets from up to four files; precedence bugs change effective config
dependencies: Filesystem read access to the candidate env paths
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: plant distinct values per file and assert the documented precedence + shadow warnings; assert server.env migration fires once and never overwrites .env.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the extra env files; explicit process env always wins over every file.

entries.name: CLI STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY auto-provisioning with existing-DB guard
entries.purpose: FACT: for commands that touch encrypted storage the CLI generates a 32-byte-hex STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY on first run and persists it to <DATA_DIR>/.env (survives upgrades; Docker-volume-aware), but refuses to generate when a storage.sqlite already exists — a new key could not decrypt existing data (guard at :222-228). This is the CLI-side genesis of the key P5 showed gates AES-256-GCM field encryption (encryption.ts).
entries.risk_class: high — key-material genesis and persistence; loss or duplication locks or splits encrypted state
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: first-run creates the key in .env; rerun with existing DB + unset key prints the refusal and generates nothing; key in .env decrypts rows written under it.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the generated key only together with the encrypted DB (P5: key loss is unrecoverable by design); restoring the previous key in DATA_DIR/.env recovers.

entries.name: Update notifier (npm registry check)
entries.purpose: FACT: an update-notifier checks npm once per 24h and prints an 'Update available' message on exit (suggesting npm install -g or omniroute update --apply), suppressed by OMNIROUTE_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER, CI, --quiet, or machine-readable --output.
entries.risk_class: low — outbound registry metadata query only
dependencies: update-notifier package (optional import, degrades when pruned)
network access to the npm registry
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: set OMNIROUTE_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 and assert no registry call/message; default path emits on exit only.
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 (env); CI/--quiet/json output auto-suppress.

entries.name: Commander program and global options
entries.purpose: FACT: createProgram builds the 'omniroute' Commander root with global --output table|json|jsonl|csv, --quiet, --no-color, --timeout, --api-key (env OMNIROUTE_API_KEY), --base-url (env OMNIROUTE_BASE_URL), --context, and --lang, then registers every command family.
entries.risk_class: low — option parsing only
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `--output json` yields machine output for any API-backed command; env-var options resolve without flags.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No state; options are per-invocation.

entries.name: Hand-written command registry (~80 register functions)
entries.purpose: FACT: registerCommands wires ~80 hand-written command modules covering server lifecycle (serve/stop/restart), management (providers/keys/combos/models/quota/cache/logs/status/doctor/config), data (backup/restore/sync/env), agent-adjacent (mcp/a2a/skills/memory/cloud/tunnel/plugin — P7 surfaces), client setup (setup-codex/claude/cursor/... 15 files), and utilities (update/open/launch/run/tray/autostart/repl).
entries.risk_class: low — registration wiring; risk lives in the individual commands
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `omniroute --help` lists every family; each register* has a corresponding bin/cli/commands/*.mjs module (grep-verified).
entries.rollback_or_disable: No state; removing a register line un-exposes a command.

entries.name: Generated OpenAPI `api` command family
entries.purpose: FACT: a second, AUTO-GENERATED command tree (`omniroute api ...`) is produced from docs/openapi.yaml by generate-api-commands.mjs (build:cli-api), covering 31 tags (playground, memory, chat, responses, providers, api-keys, quota, cloud, agentbridge, agent-skills, ...) — direct REST access mirroring the management API, including P7-class agent surfaces.
entries.risk_class: medium — generated write-capable API access from the shell incl. agent-surface tags
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: regenerate from the spec and diff (determinism); spot-call a read-only tag and assert parity with the HTTP API.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not run build:cli-api; the hand-written commands (CAP-P8-017) remain.

entries.name: CLI data-dir resolution (DATA_DIR > legacy/XDG/platform default)
entries.purpose: FACT: resolveDataDir honors DATA_DIR, else an existing ~/.omniroute legacy dir, else %APPDATA%/omniroute (win32), $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/omniroute, or ~/.omniroute; resolveStoragePath pins storage.sqlite inside it. The server-side schedule job imports this exact resolver so CLI and server agree on backup-schedule.json location (backupScheduleJob.ts:13).
entries.risk_class: low — path resolution only, but every CLI data touch flows through it
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: matrix-test each precedence branch (DATA_DIR set, legacy dir present, XDG set, win32 APPDATA).
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset DATA_DIR/XDG_CONFIG_HOME to return to the default dir.

entries.name: CLI field-encryption helper (shared format with the server)
entries.purpose: FACT: the CLI carries its own AES-256-GCM credential encryptor using the same enc:v1: prefix, 16-byte pinned auth tag, and static salt 'omniroute-field-encryption-v1' as the server (P5 encryption.ts:30-41,128) so credentials written by CLI setup commands remain decryptable by the dashboard/server and vice versa; key = scrypt(STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY), null (no-op) when unset — the same plaintext-passthrough default P5 flagged.
entries.risk_class: medium — crypto parity code; divergence silently corrupts cross-tool credential reads
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: encrypt via CLI, decrypt via server (and inverse) on a shared DATA_DIR; assert enc:v1 format and tag-pinning rejection of truncated tags.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY → helper no-ops (plaintext passthrough, matching P5's AVAILABLE-DISABLED posture).

entries.name: serve command (default) with daemon mode
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute serve` (the default command) spawns the Next standalone server as a child process — supervised in the foreground by default, or detached with --daemon writing a server PID file; flags cover --port, --no-open, --log, --no-recovery, --max-restarts, and tray toggles.
entries.risk_class: medium — spawns and supervises the long-running traffic-plane process
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `serve --daemon` then `status`/port probe; `stop` cleanly kills child+supervisor (stop.mjs:27-38 kills the supervisor too, #9455).
entries.rollback_or_disable: `omniroute stop` (SIGTERM to server and supervisor PIDs); PID files cleaned on exit.

entries.name: ServerSupervisor crash-restart policy + stop/restart lifecycle
entries.purpose: FACT: runWithSupervisor wraps the server in ServerSupervisor (pid file 'supervisor', configurable maxRestarts default 2, crash-log ring, MITM-crash detection, port-free wait per supervisorPolicy imports), with SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup; `stop` and `restart` complete the lifecycle trio over the same PID-file machinery (utils/pid.mjs).
entries.risk_class: medium — automatic process resurrection can mask crash loops; bounded by maxRestarts
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: kill the child N>maxRestarts times and assert the supervisor exits instead of restarting (shouldExitInsteadOfRestart); stop during a restart window still cleans up.
entries.rollback_or_disable: `--no-recovery` disables supervision; `--max-restarts 0` bounds it; `stop` tears everything down.

entries.name: dashboard command (browser opener)
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute dashboard` opens http://localhost:<port> (default 20128) in the system browser via the 'open' package with platform fallbacks (open/rundll32/xdg-open), or prints the URL with --url.
entries.risk_class: low — local browser launch only
dependencies: A running server for the opened URL to resolve
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: `--url` prints the computed URL; opener falls back per-platform when 'open' is unavailable.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No state; use --url in headless environments.

entries.name: Interactive TUI dashboard (ink)
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute dashboard --tui` starts a React-ink terminal dashboard (bin/cli/tui/Dashboard.jsx plus tabs/Repl.jsx/EvalWatch.jsx/OAuthFlow.jsx companions) against the local server's API with the global api-key/base-url.
entries.risk_class: low — terminal UI client of the management API
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: launch --tui against a fixture server; tabs render and honor --output/--api-key globals.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Opt-in flag; default remains the browser opener (CAP-P8-023).

entries.name: CLI tray control + platform tray runtimes
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute tray` controls a system-tray presence via platform backends (systray on unix via traySystray, native PowerShell/tray.ps1 path on Windows via trayWindows, detachedTray for background), with trayRuntime shared by serve --tray.
entries.risk_class: low — desktop shell integration, spawns platform tray helpers
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: tray show/hide/status round-trip on each supported platform; serve --tray detaches into the tray.
entries.rollback_or_disable: `omniroute tray hide`/stop; serve --no-tray; no tray started by default in headless use.

entries.name: autostart command (host boot persistence)
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute autostart enable|disable|toggle|status` manages login-time persistence of the server/tray (electron/main.js:927 shows the freedesktop .desktop-file variant written by the desktop app) — a host-configuration mutation outside the OmniRoute data dir.
entries.risk_class: medium — writes host autostart entries (persistence beyond the app)
dependencies: OS-specific autostart mechanism (xdg autostart / Windows registry / launchd)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: enable then reboot/login and observe start; status reflects the written entry; disable removes it byte-identically.
entries.rollback_or_disable: `omniroute autostart disable` removes the entry; default is no autostart entry.

entries.name: Self-update via npm (omniroute update)
entries.purpose: FACT: `omniroute update` compares the running version against `npm view omniroute version --prefer-online`, backs up bin/ to ~/.omniroute/backups first, then execSyncs `npm install -g omniroute@latest --include=optional` and trust-but-verifies by re-reading the running binary's version to catch PATH-shadowing (#9475). For HX this bypasses governor-managed change control — preliminary disposition AVAILABLE-DISABLED pending owner policy (updates should flow through the ledger/rollback path, not self-update).
entries.risk_class: high — network-driven replacement of the installed runtime in place
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: --check exit codes (0 current / 1 outdated); --dry-run prints the plan; post-update version re-read must match.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Pre-update bin backup at ~/.omniroute/backups/omniroute-<ts> (createBackup :58-80); bin/rollback.sh covers release-level rollback (CAP-P8-033).

entries.name: CLI backup create (plaintext by default) — P5 edge assessed
entries.purpose: FACT (P5 edge — CLI-side assessment): `omniroute backup [create]` copies storage.sqlite (via the SQLite online backup API, backupSqliteFile), settings.json, combos.json, and providers.json into <DATA_DIR>/backups/omniroute-backup-<ts|name>/ and writes backup-info.json. Without --encrypt the copies are PLAINTEXT (copyFileSync :231) — confirming and sharpening P5's finding: the plaintext-artifact exposure exists in the CLI path too, and these backups include the credential-bearing storage.sqlite/settings.json outside the server's db_backups retention domain. Retention and --exclude are supported; name/backupId are path-sanitized (:185, :426).
entries.risk_class: high — plaintext snapshots of credential-bearing state files land in a second, less-governed directory
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: create a backup against a fixture DATA_DIR; diff contents; confirm .enc naming only under --encrypt; confirm retention prune keeps N newest.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the backup directory; no server state is mutated by creation. Plaintext artifacts must be purged with secure deletion where they landed.

entries.name: CLI backup --encrypt (AES-256-GCM, scrypt passphrase)
entries.purpose: FACT (P5 edge): --encrypt encrypts each backed-up file with AES-256-GCM, key = scryptSync(passphrase, 16-byte random salt), output format salt(16)+iv(12)+authTag(16)+ciphertext (:131-154), files renamed <name>.enc (:218); passphrase comes from --key-file or an interactive prompt (no prompt -> exit 1). Distinct from the server's field encryption: a separate, passphrase-based file-level scheme local to this command.
entries.risk_class: medium — passphrase quality is the only protection; key-file handling on disk
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: encrypted backup bytes differ across runs (random salt/iv); wrong passphrase fails GCM auth on any future decrypt; .enc files contain no plaintext header.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the .enc artifacts; without the passphrase they are unrecoverable ciphertext (see CAP-P8-906 gap: the CLI itself cannot restore them).

entries.name: CLI backup --cloud upload client (dead server counterpart)
entries.purpose: FACT (P5 edge): --cloud uploads the finished backup directory as multipart/form-data to the RUNNING server's /api/db-backups/cloud with Bearer OMNIROUTE_API_KEY + CLI-token headers, 30s timeout, warning-only on failure. Grep-verified across src/ and bin/: the ONLY occurrence of 'db-backups/cloud' is this client line — no server route exists in the pinned corpus (src/app/api/db-backups/ = export, exportAll, import, route.ts with no cloud handler), so the upload always fails closed with a warning. This answers P5's CAP-P5-036 pointer: cloud execution exists CLI-side, but its server endpoint is NOT-ESTABLISHED (CAP-P8-905).
entries.risk_class: high — would exfiltrate full state snapshots (plaintext unless combined with --encrypt) to whatever the base-url points at, if the endpoint existed
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: point --base-url at a fixture host and observe the 404/warning path; assert no local mutation on failure; if an endpoint ever lands, re-test with/without --encrypt.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not pass --cloud; failure is warning-only and the local backup remains. No server-side artifact is created today (endpoint absent).

entries.name: Scheduled backup job executing the CLI implementation in-process
entries.purpose: FACT (P5 edge closed): the server's backup-schedule job imports runBackupCommand and resolveDataDir DIRECTLY from bin/cli (no spawn) and runs the persisted backup-schedule.json (written by `omniroute backup auto enable`) on a 30s tick with cron match, same-minute dedup, and lastRunAt persistence. encrypt:true schedules are REFUSED with an explicit error because no non-interactive passphrase source exists (`auto enable` has no --key-file) — an honest fail-closed guard rather than a stdin hang (:82-88). cloud:true schedules would run the upload into the same absent endpoint as CAP-P8-030 (warning-only).
entries.risk_class: medium — server-triggered disk writes on a cron; encrypt schedules silently never produce backups (refused)
dependencies: server job scheduler running (P7 jobs posture)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: write a schedule with a past cron, tick runBackupScheduleTick(now), assert exactly one run per minute; encrypt:true returns false and logs the refusal.
entries.rollback_or_disable: `omniroute backup auto disable` flips enabled:false; deleting backup-schedule.json stops the job entirely (readSchedule null-guards).

entries.name: CLI restore command — and the encrypted-restore gap
entries.purpose: FACT (P5 edge): `omniroute restore <id>` lists backups and, after confirmation, copyFileSync's the four well-known filenames back into DATA_DIR (:451-459) with id path-sanitization (:426). GAP: createDecipheriv is imported (:13) but never used anywhere in the module — no decrypt path exists, and the restore loop only matches the PLAINTEXT filenames, so a backup created with --encrypt (files named *.enc) restores NOTHING while still printing 'restored' (:460). Encrypted CLI backups are write-only with this tool — a data-recovery trap P5's server-side restore (integrity-checked, pre-restore snapshot) does not share. INFERENCE (labeled): the mismatch is an unfinished feature, not a deliberate refusal.
entries.risk_class: high — a restore that silently restores nothing is a data-integrity hazard exactly at incident time
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: round-trip plaintext backup -> restore -> diff; then encrypt a backup and run restore — assert zero files restored (the gap), deterministically.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Restore overwrites DATA_DIR files without a pre-restore snapshot (unlike the server path, P5 backup.ts:413-430) — take bin/snapshot-data.sh first (CAP-P8-033).

entries.name: Ops shell scripts: rollback / snapshot-data / restore-data / restore-policies
entries.purpose: FACT: bash incident-recovery tooling shipped in bin/: rollback.sh (npm re-install of a previous version, or docker re-tag + compose recreate), snapshot-data.sh (consistent VACUUM INTO point-in-time snapshot of the SQLite volume, prints a snapshot id), restore-data.sh (pre-restore safety snapshot + verification + refusal to run unattended without --yes), restore-policies.sh, all sharing _ops-common.sh. These are the deploy/data-layer rollback surfaces the work order's rollback discipline maps to.
entries.risk_class: high — data-volume overwrite and version-replacement tooling; correct by design (snapshots first) but destructive if misused
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: snapshot -> mutate fixture DB -> restore -> byte-compare; rollback --method docker against a fixture tag.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Self-hedging: restore-data takes a pre-restore snapshot of current data before overwriting (:6-8 header); rollback.sh itself is the release-level inverse.

entries.name: Recovery tools: reset-password and reset-encrypted-columns
entries.purpose: FACT: two break-glass tools bypass Commander: omniroute-reset-password (own bin entry; interactive or --password-stdin; updates the admin password directly in the DB) and reset-encrypted-columns (recovery for broken encrypted credential columns — the CLI front-end of the class P5 found server-side as recovery.ts, LAB-ONLY there). Both require local DB access — the intended attacker-model boundary.
entries.risk_class: high — direct credential/DB mutation outside the authenticated management plane
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: on a fixture DB, reset the password and authenticate with the new one; run reset-encrypted-columns against a fixture with a deliberately wrong STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
entries.rollback_or_disable: No inverse — credential overwrite; mitigate by pre-running bin/snapshot-data.sh (CAP-P8-033).

entries.name: setup-* client-integration writers (15 tools)
entries.purpose: FACT: fifteen setup-* commands (codex, claude, cline, continue, crush, cursor, goose, kilo, open-code/opencode, qwen, roo, aider, plus generic setup) write OmniRoute connection configuration INTO third-party AI CLI tools' own config files — outbound mutation of other applications' state from the OmniRoute CLI.
entries.risk_class: medium — writes foreign tool configs on the host (clobber risk outside OmniRoute's data dir)
dependencies: The target tool's config directory present
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: run each setup-* against a sandboxed HOME; diff the written config; re-run for idempotence.
entries.rollback_or_disable: Manual: each tool's config must be reverted by editing/removing the written block — no uninstall path found for setup-* writes (INFERENCE from command inventory; none registered).

entries.name: --mcp stdio entry mechanics (cross-reference to P7)
entries.purpose: FACT: the CLI doubles as the MCP-server launcher — `--mcp` anywhere in argv diverts to bin/mcp-server.mjs startMcpCli after installing the stdout-guard, entirely bypassing Commander. P8 ledgers only the entry/packaging mechanics; the MCP server itself (~107 tools, disabled-by-default posture) is P7's CAP-P7-001…006 with its control-plane-collision notes. Collision note: exposing the agent surface is one argv token away in the shipped binary.
entries.risk_class: medium — one-flag activation of the full MCP agent surface from the shipped bin
